clue.text: Tense journalist chasing beer with short is stupid

blocks.note: a half is a half-pint of beer
W is the standard abbreviation for with
It is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it, and a short is a small measure of spirits
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter knocking back beer and spirits gets visibly dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' puts the tense and the journalist after the drinks, as a chaser follows a drink. HALF-WITTED is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone said to have only half their wits is foolish or dim, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Securer when covered by hire purchase

indicators.note: something covered by another thing sits inside it, wrapped by the outer letters

blocks.note: HP is the British abbreviation for buying on instalments
as in as I left, meaning when I left

explanation.surface: Something bought on credit secures a loan, it suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: Hire purchase is the British name for paying in instalments, abbreviated HP.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasp is a hinged metal fastening for a door or lid, which secures it, usually with a padlock.

clue.text: Chattering incessantly, yellow bird south of wood

blocks.note: a log is a piece of wood
or is gold or yellow in heraldry
a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A yellow bird chirps nonstop below a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, south of means placed below, so the bird and its colour come after the wood. This is the American spelling, LOGORRHEA; British usage adds an O, logorrhoea.
explanation.definitionFit: Logorrhoea is an excessive flow of talk, so it is a noun for nonstop chatter.

clue.text: James's work with innovative AI makes hit novel

indicators.note: novel means new and original, so the letters are made into something fresh

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
innovative means new
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A book written with artificial intelligence becomes a bestseller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' is a link, but 'makes hit' is also part of the letters. 'Novel' is both the anagram signal and a hint at the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: What Maisie Knew is an 1897 novel by Henry James, so it is one of James's works.

clue.text: Historian occasionally looking up Asquith is crafty

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter is kept
in a down answer, looking up means the letters run upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A historian sometimes admires the wily political skill of the prime minister Asquith.
explanation.walkthrough: H. H. Asquith was the British prime minister from 1908 to 1916, but he is only part of the letters. SUTICAT read upwards is TACITUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman writer whose Annals and Histories chronicle the early emperors.

clue.text: English partners defending mostly equal sides

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
level means equal, as in level scores
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: English partners on a sports pitch hold out for a near draw.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are named by compass point, and North and South play as a pair. 'Defending' here only places the partners behind the equal word, as defenders stand behind. That gives ELEVENS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football team has eleven players, so teams are called elevens, as sides are.

clue.text: Weed this writer's spotted in middle of cowpat

indicators.note: something spotted in a place is seen sitting inside it, so one piece sits within another
only the central letters of the following word are wanted, not the whole of it

blocks.note: the two centre letters of this six-letter word
the setter says I am, contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being seen standing in a cowpat, presumably while weeding a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' looks like a plant but means a feeble person, the WIMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed is slang for a weak, puny person, and so is a wimp.

clue.text: Old people online civil in retirement? Not entirely

indicators.note: someone in retirement has withdrawn or gone back, so the letters run backwards
not entirely means only part of the phrase, so the answer lies within it

blocks.note: these letters run inside the phrase, read backwards

explanation.surface: Pensioners who go online in retirement are only partly well-mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people' seems to mean pensioners, which fits 'retirement'. It actually means an ancient people, a tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe, led by Boudicca, so a people from long ago.

clue.text: Vegetables spoil pies – stop it!

indicators.note: to spoil something is to mess it up, so the letters get scrambled

blocks.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone protests that vegetables ruin a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' reads as a verb with vegetables as its subject, but it is the anagram signal for the next words.
explanation.definitionFit: Petits pois are small, sweet young garden peas, a vegetable.

clue.text: Taking a drug out of Java, perhaps?

definitions.text: Taking a drug out of Java, perhaps?

blocks.clueFragment: Taking a drug out of Java, perhaps?
blocks.note: surface reading: smuggling narcotics out of the Indonesian island
setter's reading: java is slang for coffee, and the drug is the stimulant it contains

explanation.walkthrough: Java the island suggests drug smuggling. Java is also American slang for coffee, and caffeine counts as a drug. The answer is DECAFFEINATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing decaf coffee means stripping the stimulant from the beans, a chemical removal process.

clue.text: Character from abroad returning before twelve US soldiers

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: the morning hours, before noon, are a.m.
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A foreign figure comes home just ahead of a dozen American troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve' tempts you towards a number, but before twelve o'clock is the morning, and the clock abbreviation is what's wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign written character.

clue.text: Most intelligent student charging about mountain

blocks.note: c. (circa) is the abbreviation for about
L is the learner driver's plate, the crossword's usual student
the world's highest mountain

explanation.surface: A bright pupil storms up a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants the student charging up the mountain. In the wordplay, 'charging' only joins the student to the mountain, and the circa abbreviation goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever means intelligent, so the superlative form means most intelligent.

clue.text: Might one make you feel better with a floral bouquet?

definitions.text: Might one make you feel better with a floral bouquet?

blocks.clueFragment: Might one make you feel better with a floral bouquet?
blocks.note: surface reading: a friend bringing flowers to cheer up someone who is ill
setter's reading: bouquet is a scent, so this is a healer working with flowery smells and oils

explanation.walkthrough: A bouquet is a bunch of flowers but also a fragrance, as in a wine's bouquet. The answer is AROMATHERAPIST.
explanation.definitionFit: This practitioner treats clients with scented plant oils, claiming the fragrances improve wellbeing.

clue.text: Do radio bit somehow prompter

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put together in a new order

blocks.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A presenter is urged to manage a radio segment somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio suggests broadcasting, which fits the definition, but the clue's words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot board is a television slang name for a cue card or autocue that feeds a presenter lines.

clue.text: Part of windmill contained rolls and bloomers

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns round, so the combined letters run backwards

blocks.note: a windmill's sails are its turning arms
to contain something is to have it

explanation.surface: A windmill's sail once held bread rolls and a pair of old-fashioned knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' suggests underwear. Here it means flowers, things that bloom. SAIL HAD read backwards is DAHLIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahlias are garden plants grown for their showy flowers, so they are literally things that bloom.

clue.text: Liberal beat Ford?

blocks.note: liberal in the sense of lenient, not strict
to top a rival is to beat them

explanation.surface: It reads like a political headline about a Liberal defeating someone named Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford is the car maker, not a politician; the question mark shows a Ford is only one example of a SOFT TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft top is a convertible car with a folding fabric roof, and some Ford models were sold that way.

clue.text: Temporary shelter erected to protect fish trap at sea

indicators.note: something erected is set upright, so in a down answer the letters go bottom to top
to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a tent is a portable, temporary shelter
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A makeshift shelter is put up to guard a fish trap out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like a noun but is the verb. The upturned shelter splits after its first letter to let the verb inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle net is a fishing net that catches fish by entangling them, so a trap used at sea.

clue.text: Award puts out second hip American music producer

indicators.note: to put something out is to eject it, so the named letter leaves the word

blocks.note: the Hollywood film prize
s is the abbreviation for second
fashionable, as in the in thing
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An awards ceremony sidelines its runner-up in favour of a trendy American record producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests someone in a studio. It is really something that produces music, an instrument, the OCARINA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, so literally a thing that makes music.

clue.text: Article on excellent pub coming up, "Knight & Horse"

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means the letters rise, running from bottom to top

blocks.note: the indefinite article
A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I for the digit
a bar is a pub
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A write-up of a fine pub, the Knight and Horse, sounds like a pub-guide entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted pub name is a decoy: Knight is wordplay, using the chess abbreviation, and Horse alone is the definition. Only the middle pair is reversed; the article stays on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian is a famous breed of horse, prized for its speed and stamina.

clue.text: Affected area initially itching, mostly red

indicators.note: letters that have been affected are altered, so they are rearranged
initially points to the very start of the word before it, keeping just its opening letter
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
this word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A patch of skin, itchy at first, has gone largely red, like a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: The skin-and-rash picture hides a wine: 'red' is the definition, and 'affected' signals rearranging the letters, not a symptom.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a Tuscan wine, and red is everyday shorthand for red wine.

clue.text: Queen delighted by this jazz fan with a vast sum of money?

blocks.note: cat is old jazz slang for an enthusiast
a mint is a huge amount of money

explanation.surface: The monarch would enjoy a jazz-loving millionaire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen is not royalty: a queen is a female cat. Cats famously love this plant, the CATMINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Catmint, or catnip, is a plant whose scent excites cats, including a female cat called a queen.

clue.text: Provisions are disposed of at morning meeting here?

definitions.text: Provisions are disposed of at morning meeting here?

blocks.clueFragment: Provisions are disposed of at morning meeting
blocks.note: surface reading: supplies are dealt with at a business meeting held in the morning
setter's reading: the place where food is eaten when the household gathers for the first meal of the day

explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed of' sounds like admin. Here it means eaten, and the morning meeting is the family's first meal. The answer is BREAKFAST TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The household sits round this piece of furniture each morning to eat, getting through the food supplies.

clue.text: Cross old man visiting alien living in exile

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so these letters enter the other piece

blocks.note: the extra-terrestrial of the Spielberg film
a cross is the letter X
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: An angry father calls on a foreigner who has been banished from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the letter shaped like a cross; the alien is the film character, split to receive the visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat, an expatriate, lives abroad away from their homeland, as an exile does.

clue.text: Reportedly takes home containers for drinks

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: to take home pay is to earn it

explanation.surface: Someone apparently brings home flasks.
explanation.walkthrough: Take-home pay is what you earn. In a non-rhotic British accent, earns and URNS sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea and coffee urns are large metal vessels for serving hot drinks.

clue.text: A tipple in breaks?

indicators.note: letters that break apart can be put back together in a different order

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: It sounds like having a drink during work breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the letters of 'a tipple in' break up to make a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An appletini is an apple-flavoured martini cocktail, a tipple in its own right.

clue.text: Private Victor Watts has deserted

indicators.note: whoever has deserted has left their post, so those letters are missing

blocks.note: a victor is the one who wins
W is the symbol for watts

explanation.surface: A soldier, Private Victor Watts, has gone AWOL.
explanation.walkthrough: Private, Victor and Watts all read as a soldier's rank and name. Private is the definition, and the others are wordplay. WINNER without W gives INNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner feelings or thoughts are private ones, kept hidden from other people.

clue.text: Saw cut fruit

indicators.note: a word that is cut is trimmed short, losing its final letter

blocks.note: past tense of see, in the sense of going out with someone romantically

explanation.surface: A saw slices through a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the tool, but it is the past tense of see, as in seeing someone romantically.
explanation.definitionFit: The date is the sweet brown fruit of the date palm.

clue.text: Around one, bizarrely, a Sting set begins

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the single letter
done bizarrely means done in a strange way, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A concert by the singer Sting kicks off strangely, built around a single number.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting the rock singer is a red herring. His name is just letters to rearrange around the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to set it going, so instigates means starts or begins.
